Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. High level: Redwood's standard approach is to vest onboarding credits over 90 days and apply a 180-day clawback window tied to net churn (i.e., if the customer cancels entirely within 180 days, credits are reclaimed via true-up). That said, I'm happy to make the language explicit and propose a smoothing matrix that avoids surprise retroactive adjustments.

Proposal (summary):
- Onboarding credits shall be applied to invoices pro rata over the first 90 days following go-live.
- If subscription termination occurs within 180 days of go-live, remaining unallocated credits are subject to a one-time true-up and reversal.
- The smoothing/offset matrix in Appendix B applies only to partial monthly usage variances and does not trigger retroactive chargebacks beyond the 180-day clawback window.

I'll loop in Legal and Finance to produce a redline and the PDF illustration for the matrix.

Attaching a quick note and will send the redline in the next message.

Sofia / Ben / Jordan,

Thanks for the clear framing. I've reviewed the attached redline and propose the following refinements so the contract language is unambiguous and minimizes operational edge cases:

1) Define 'Go-Live' explicitly: "Go-Live means the date on which Customer's production environment begins routine use of the Services as mutually confirmed in writing." This avoids disputes about trial periods.

2) Vesting mechanics (clean clause): "Onboarding Credits provided under Exhibit A shall be amortized and applied to Customer invoices on a pro rata basis over the 90-day period beginning on the Go-Live date (the 'Vesting Period')."

3) Clawback / True-up (precise): "If Customer terminates the Subscription for convenience, or if the Subscription terminates for cause attributable to Customer, prior to the expiration of 180 days from the Go-Live date (the 'Clawback Window'), Redwood may recoup unamortized Onboarding Credits by offset against amounts otherwise owed during the next invoice cycle. Redemption or offset shall not be applied retroactively beyond the Clawback Window."

4) Smoothing matrix intent: we'll add an explanatory paragraph in Appendix B: "The Smoothing Matrix in Appendix B addresses month-to-month usage volatility and shall not be interpreted as creating additional retroactive billing adjustments beyond the Clawback Window; any adjustments under Appendix B will be prospectively applied."

Operational notes for Ben: please confirm our billing platform can flag Go-Live and automatically amortize credits across the 90-day window, and confirm the mechanics for offsetting within the next invoice cycle if clawback is triggered.

Jordan — if those points are OK from Acme's perspective we'll incorporate them verbatim into Exhibit A and return a redline for signature.
